_why: The window each clip is read at in the runner's nightly (the EP's decision of 2026-11-14: a runner cannot read a whole clip, so each clip is read as a window at its worst moment, collapse at 60 ticks; the full reading stays a local run on Orb's PC). skip is run-pixels.mjs's --skip (ticks run without a picture first; the window starts at tick skip + 1). A clip with no entry is read from tick 1 for defaultTicks, the speed trial's way. 'from' says how the moment was found: an entry that has not been measured says so. tools/flash/nightly-windows.mjs --check reads this file. capMin is the clip's time cap in minutes (default defaultCapMin): the ticks skipped before a window cost time too, about 2.2 s a tick on a runner (run 43580079641: a skip of 950 plus 76 captured ticks used the 45 minutes), so a window far into a clip needs a longer cap than its captured ticks do. The analyser counts no change in the first 60 frames of a clip (its warm-up) and the two-second memory reading in the first 120, so a window needs more than 61 ticks, and about 120 ticks of lead-in before the moment it is meant to catch. Each window names what it `holds`; tools/flash/window-check.mjs (in CI) fails when the headless run no longer has that event in the window's counted part (after a clip's first 60 frames).
